method.model: MACE-MPA-0 medium (same as worker; only model cached on this machine)
method.protocol: Independent re-implementation: bulk Cu a0 relaxed (3.640 A); Cu(111) p(3x3) 4-layer slab, bottom 2 layers fixed, 16 A vacuum; O at fcc/hcp/ontop at 1/9 ML; BFGS fmax 0.005 eV/A; isolated O atom and relaxed O2 in a ~20 A orthorhombic box

payload.note:
REPRODUCTION: I wrote my own script and got fcc -4.837, hcp -4.783, ontop -3.082 eV vs the isolated O atom. Against 1/2 O2 I got fcc -1.694 eV. E(O atom) = -1.548 eV and O2 De = 6.28 eV. All of these match the worker's numbers to 1 meV. The site ordering fcc > hcp >> top holds, and the numbers converge with cell size and slab thickness as reported.
PREMISE: well-posed as a 0 K electronic binding energy, as the worker states. There is no tier1 calibration entry for this property (that file holds bulk thermophysical data), and no experiment measures it directly.
METHOD: a static slab relaxation is the right protocol, and ensemble and run length do not apply. The weak point is the isolated-O reference in an MLIP. The worker's own test answers it: De(O2) = 6.28 eV matches the well-known spin-polarized PBE overbinding of O2, which implies a PBE-like atomic O energy. This error enters E_ads directly. The worker's +/-0.6 eV band (PBE-like -4.84 to thermochemically corrected -4.30) is an honest statement of it.
LITERATURE: a web search found a DFT study of O on Cu(111) (Reddy & Chatterjee, arXiv:2505.12914). A search-engine excerpt credits it with fcc -5.000 and hcp -4.905 eV vs a gas-phase O atom, with hollow sites preferred. I could not extract the PDF text, so I have NOT confirmed that paper's functional, coverage or settings. Taken at face value, the gap is about 0.16 eV, consistent with MLIP-vs-DFT error and setup differences, and well within the stated uncertainty. The ~0.1 eV fcc-hcp gap in that excerpt matches the worker's 0.05 eV in ordering and rough size. A conference poster in the same search (Tohoku ACCMS-11) reportedly gives -6.37/-6.26 eV, but its reference and functional are unclear. I treat it as non-comparable and did not rely on it.
LIMITATIONS: only MACE-MPA-0 is cached here, so I could not run a second MLIP. My reproduction confirms the arithmetic and protocol, not the model's independence from its training data.
VERDICT: pass. The value -4.84 eV (fcc, PBE-like, 1/9 ML) is reproducible and physically sensible, and it is not contradicted by the partly confirmed literature value. Read it as a PBE-level number. The true binding is probably weaker, closer to -4.3 eV, because of the O-reference error.
